questions.q: If d_model is 64 and num_heads is 4, what is head_dim?
questions.explain: head_dim = d_model / num_heads = 64 / 4 = 16; each head operates in a 16-dimensional subspace.

questions.q: Why does multi-head attention split the embedding dimension into subspaces instead of simply running full-width attention multiple times?
options: Running full-width attention multiple times is computationally cheaper
Splitting gives each head its own learned Q/K/V projections, letting heads specialize; repeating full-width attention would just duplicate identical computation
PyTorch does not allow calling attention more than once
Splitting removes the need for a softmax
questions.explain: Each head's own projection matrices let it learn to attend to different kinds of relationships, which repeating the same full-width computation cannot provide.

questions.q: In nn.MultiheadAttention(embed_dim, num_heads, batch_first=True), what constraint must embed_dim and num_heads satisfy?
options: num_heads must be larger than embed_dim
embed_dim must be evenly divisible by num_heads
There is no constraint between them
questions.explain: PyTorch computes head_dim = embed_dim // num_heads, which requires embed_dim to divide evenly by num_heads or it raises an error.

questions.q: What does the out_proj layer inside nn.MultiheadAttention do?
options: It computes the softmax over attention scores
It combines the concatenated outputs of all heads back into one embed_dim-wide vector via a final linear layer
It splits the input into heads
questions.explain: After each head's attention output is concatenated back to embed_dim width, out_proj applies one shared linear transformation before returning the final result.

questions.q: Given input x of shape (batch, seq_len, embed_dim), what shape does nn.MultiheadAttention's attn_output have?
options: (batch, seq_len, embed_dim) -- the same shape as the input
questions.explain: Despite reshaping internally per head, the module concatenates heads back and projects to the original embed_dim, so the output shape matches the input shape.
